name: Lloyd Blankfein

summary.text: Lloyd Blankfein was chief executive of Goldman Sachs during the 2008 financial crisis and the AIG rescue. He testified on the first day of the Financial Crisis Inquiry Commission's hearings on January 13, 2010 and submitted written responses to the commission's follow-up questions. Goldman Sachs was among the counterparties paid through the New York Fed's Maiden Lane III vehicle, which SIGTARP found effectively paid AIG's counterparties par value; a March 2009 Congressional Record attachment lists Goldman at $5.6 billion in Maiden Lane III payments, and Goldman itself described $4.3 billion included in Maiden Lane III and $5.5 billion of positions outside it. In July 2010 Goldman paid $550 million to settle SEC charges over the ABACUS 2007-AC1 CDO.

facts.claim: On January 13, 2010 Blankfein testified before the Financial Crisis Inquiry Commission on the causes of the financial crisis, alongside the heads of JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America and Morgan Stanley.
facts.quote: On January 13, 2010 Lloyd Blankfein testified to the Commission on the subject of causes of the financial crisis.

sources.title: Goldman Sachs Testimony before the U.S. Financial Crisis Inquiry Commission (FCIC)
Bank CEOs Admit Mistakes at Financial Crisis Inquiry Commission Hearing

facts.claim: At the FCIC hearing Blankfein said that investors who bought mortgage-backed securities from Goldman while other parts of the bank were shorting the same instruments were professional investors who wanted that exposure; chairman Phil Angelides compared it to selling a car with faulty brakes and buying insurance on the buyer.

sources.title: Blankfein to FCIC: Asset Owners Are Professionals Who Wanted Mortgage Exposure

facts.claim: Blankfein submitted a written response, dated February 3, 2010, to the FCIC's January 28 and February 3, 2010 follow-up letters.
facts.quote: First Response to the January 28 and February 3, 2010 Letters of the Financial Crisis Inquiry Commission- Lloyd Blankfein Former CEO of Goldman Sachs Response to Hearing Follow-Up Questions

sources.title: First Response to the January 28 and February 3, 2010 Letters of the Financial Crisis Inquiry Commission - Lloyd Blankfein

facts.claim: SIGTARP's November 17, 2009 audit found that because AIG's counterparties were paid the fair market value of the underlying assets through Maiden Lane III and kept the collateral previously posted, they were effectively paid par value; a Congressional Record attachment lists Goldman Sachs at $5.6 billion in Maiden Lane III payments.
facts.quote: Because the counterparties were both paid the fair market value of the assets underlying the credit default swap contracts and permitted to keep the collateral that had previously been posted, the counterparties were effectively paid the par value of the underlying assets.

sources.publisher: SIGTARP (via FRASER, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis)
sources.title: Factors Affecting Efforts to Limit Payments to AIG Counterparties
Congressional Record, March 19, 2009, p. S3582 (AIG counterparty payments)

facts.claim: Goldman Sachs stated in response to the SIGTARP report that $4.3 billion of its AIG positions were included in Maiden Lane III and $5.5 billion were not, and quoted the report's finding that continued government backing of AIG protected Goldman against an AIG default on the remaining $5.5 billion.
facts.quote: "continued Government backing of AIG provided Goldman Sachs with ongoing protection against an AIG default on the remaining $5.5 billion."

sources.title: Goldman Sachs Responds to Questions from The New York Times about the SIGTARP Report on AIG

facts.claim: On July 15, 2010 the SEC announced that Goldman Sachs would pay $550 million ($250 million to harmed investors and a $300 million penalty) to settle charges that it failed to disclose the role of Paulson & Co. in selecting the portfolio of the ABACUS 2007-AC1 CDO; Goldman acknowledged its marketing materials contained incomplete information without admitting or denying the charges.
facts.quote: The SEC said Goldman failed to disclose to investors vital information about the CDO, known as ABACUS 2007-AC1, particularly the role that hedge fund Paulson & Co. Inc. played in the portfolio selection process.

sources.title: Goldman Sachs to Pay Record $550 Million to Settle SEC Charges Related to Subprime Mortgage CDO

connections.claim: Goldman Sachs was among the counterparties whose CDO positions were purchased through the New York Fed's Maiden Lane III vehicle, which the Fed authorized to borrow up to $30 billion.
connections.quote: The Federal Reserve Board authorized FRBNY to lend up to $30 billion to Maiden Lane III, a newly formed limited liability company.

openQuestions: Site claim that AIG's March 2009 disclosure listed $12.9 billion to Goldman Sachs across collateral, Maiden Lane III and securities lending: not confirmed; sources found give $5.6 billion (Maiden Lane III) and Goldman's own $4.3 billion / $5.5 billion split, which are different measures.
Site description of Blankfein as 'one of the largest recipients of AIG rescue pass-through payments': the payments went to Goldman Sachs as a firm; no source ties them to Blankfein personally.
Blankfein's tenure dates as CEO (2006-2018) were not confirmed from a source found here.
